# Bilingual product notes: from idea to roadmap

This document is written in a mix of English and Spanish, the way many
teams actually write their product notes. It collects lessons about
moving from an idea to a roadmap.

## Starting with the problem

Every good product starts with a problem, not a solution. Describe the
problem in plain words: quién lo padece, en qué momento y qué costo
tiene no resolverlo. If the problem statement is vague, the roadmap
will be vague too.

## Prioritizing the backlog

The backlog is not a wish list. Each item should carry a hypothesis:
what we believe, how we will measure it, and what we will learn if we
are wrong. Teams that skip the hypothesis end up building features
without learning anything.

El backlog ordenado por impacto permite decidir qué se construye y qué
se descarta. Una buena regla es preguntar: ¿resuelve esto un problema
real de un usuario real? Si la respuesta es no, la historia vuelve a la
pila.

## From roadmap to delivery

The roadmap communicates the plan; the delivery plan communicates the
commitment. Separate the two. El roadmap mira al trimestre, el plan de
entrega mira al sprint. Confusing them is the fastest way to lose
trust with stakeholders.

## Measuring success

Define the north star metric early. Everything else is a supporting
metric. La métrica principal responde a la pregunta: ¿estamos
resolviendo el problema que dijimos que íbamos a resolver? When the
north star moves, the team learns; when it stays flat, the hypothesis
was wrong.

## Conclusion

Bilingual product notes are a reality of distributed teams. The
important thing is not the language but the structure: problem,
hypothesis, backlog, roadmap and metrics. El idioma importa menos que
la claridad.
